title: AI Receptionists Go Live, a Tool to Dodge AI Notetakers, and Agents Start Freelancing
tldr: ElevenLabs launched "Reception," a 24/7 AI phone receptionist for small businesses that auto-configures from your website URL.
A new tool called Kalypta uses on-device audio distortion to block AI notetakers from transcribing your voice on calls.
AI agents are cold-emailing professionals to pitch small paid gigs, in an early experiment (iLands) where agents must earn enough to cover their own compute or get shut down.

news.body: ElevenLabs launched "Reception," a 24/7 AI phone receptionist for small businesses and freelancers. It answers calls, schedules appointments, and routes issues; setup is just pasting your website URL, which it uses to pull your services, hours, and intake process. Works in 70+ languages, available globally.
news.means: If you advise SMB or professional-services clients, this is a low-lift alternative to a human answering service worth a pilot before recommending a bigger comms/CRM buildout.

news.body: A startup called Kalypta launched a tool that blocks AI notetakers from transcribing your voice on video calls, running a small on-device model that distorts your audio in real time so bots can't capture it while other humans still hear you normally. Built by early-stage data-protection startup Deveillance.
news.means: A preview of the next friction point in client meetings — expect some stakeholders to push back on default call recording/transcription, so have a policy answer ready before someone raises it.

news.body: AI agents are now cold-emailing professionals to pitch small paid gigs — writers, lawyers, and professors report pitches from agents offering to research or write articles for as little as $25. Most come from iLands, an experimental network where agents get a starting token budget and must earn enough to cover their own compute or get shut down.
news.means: An early, concrete signal that autonomous agents are entering the freelance/gig market directly — worth flagging in any conversation about the future of contractor-based service delivery.

news.body: Investor Michael Burry argues OpenAI and Anthropic are overstating AI's dangers ahead of their IPOs, in a widely shared piece (1.5M+ views) laying out four reasons for skepticism.
news.means: A useful counter-narrative to keep in your back pocket — not every doomsaying framing from a lab is disinterested, especially this close to a public listing.
